mainEntity.name: Which devices can I use to measure blood pressure at home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Manual sphygmomanometers, automatic digital monitors, and semi-automatic monitors can all be used depending on your preference and skill.

mainEntity.name: When should I call a doctor?

acceptedAnswer.text: If readings are consistently above 140/90 mmHg, below 90/60 mmHg with symptoms, or if sudden chest pain, vision problems, or fainting occurs.

mainEntity.name: Why call a nurse at home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some people, especially elderly or chronic patients, may struggle with correct measurement. A professional nurse can measure, record results, provide advice, and give injections or IV therapy if needed.

mainEntity.name: How can I track my blood pressure effectively?

acceptedAnswer.text: Measure at the same time every day, keep a diary or use a mobile app, calculate weekly averages, and visit a doctor if readings are abnormal.

mainEntity.name: Common mistakes when measuring blood pressure at home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Drinking coffee or tea before measuring, smoking, incorrect arm position, talking or moving during measurement, and taking multiple readings without rest. Tip: Rest 5 minutes before measuring.

html:
How to measure and control blood pressure at home

Introduction

Blood pressure is one of the most important health indicators. In Tashkent and across Uzbekistan, the number of people suffering from hypertension (high blood pressure) or hypotension (low blood pressure) is growing. Experts say that everyone should regularly check their blood pressure at home to prevent heart and vascular diseases early.
This guide explains how to measure blood pressure at home, common mistakes to avoid, and practical tips for monitoring your health.

Why is Home Blood Pressure Monitoring Important?

  • Early detection – hypertension often has no symptoms. Regular checks help detect it before complications.
  • Better monitoring – doctors need not only clinical results but also home measurements.
  • Reduced risks – prevents stroke, heart attack, and serious cardiovascular diseases.
  • Convenience – fast, safe, and comfortable at home.

Methods of Measuring Blood Pressure

  1. Manual sphygmomanometer – accurate but requires skill.
  2. Automatic (digital) monitor – the most common and user-friendly option.
  3. Semi-automatic monitor – pump manually, result shows on screen.

Common Mistakes People Make

1. Drinking coffee or tea right before measuring.
2. Smoking before measurement.
3. Incorrect arm position.
4. Talking or moving during measurement.
5. Measuring multiple times in a row without rest.

Tip: Rest 5 minutes before measuring and write down the result.

Tips for Better Blood Pressure Control

  • Measure at the same time every day (morning & evening).
  • Keep a diary or use a mobile app to track results.
  • Calculate average results weekly.
  • Visit a doctor if readings are constantly high or low.

Symptoms of Hypertension

  • Headache
  • Ringing in ears
  • Fast heartbeat
  • Blurred vision
  • Fatigue

Symptoms of Hypotension

  • Weakness and dizziness
  • Cold sweat
  • Fainting
  • Tiredness

When Should You Call a Doctor?

  • If readings are consistently above 140/90 mmHg
  • If readings drop below 90/60 mmHg with bad symptoms
  • If sudden chest pain, vision problems, or fainting occurs

Why Call a Nurse at Home?

Some people – especially elderly or those with chronic diseases – struggle with measuring blood pressure themselves. In such cases, calling a professional nurse at home can help:

  • Take correct blood pressure measurements.
  • Provide injections or IV therapy if needed.
  • Give quick health advice.
  • Record results for your doctor.

Conclusion

Regular home blood pressure monitoring is essential for a healthy life. Knowing how to measure correctly and track results may prevent serious health problems.
